title: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP
text: The ARPANET adopted the TCP/IP protocols, so that separate computer networks could talk to one another. This switch is often described as the birth of the modern Internet.

title: Watt patents the separate condenser
text: James Watt received a patent for a steam engine with a separate condenser, which wasted far less fuel than earlier engines.

title: Galileo spots moons around Jupiter
text: Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope at Jupiter and noticed small 'stars' beside it. Over the following nights he realised they were moons orbiting the planet.

title: The first iPhone is unveiled
text: Steve Jobs presented the first iPhone, which combined a phone, a music player and an internet device with a touch screen.

title: First insulin treatment of a patient
text: Fourteen-year-old Leonard Thompson, who had diabetes, was given an injection of insulin extract in Toronto. His blood sugar fell, and insulin went on to become a life-saving medicine.

title: Apple introduces the Macintosh
text: The Macintosh brought windows, icons and a mouse to ordinary home and office users.

title: Edison's electric lamp patent
text: Thomas Edison was granted a US patent for his incandescent electric lamp with a carbon filament, a step towards practical electric lighting.

title: Benz applies for a motor-car patent
text: Karl Benz applied for a patent for his Motorwagen, a three-wheeled vehicle with a petrol engine that is often regarded as the first practical car.

title: Gravitational waves detected
text: Scientists of the LIGO and Virgo collaborations announced the first direct detection of gravitational waves, ripples in space-time that Einstein had predicted a century earlier.

title: Two telephone filings on the same day
text: Alexander Graham Bell and Elisha Gray each took telephone paperwork to the patent office on the same day, one reason the telephone's invention is still a famous dispute.

title: YouTube.com is registered
text: The domain name youtube.com was registered, the start of the website that would change how the world watches video.

title: Pluto is discovered
text: Clyde Tombaugh found Pluto at Lowell Observatory by comparing photographs of the night sky taken on different dates.

title: First steam locomotive journey on rails
text: Richard Trevithick's locomotive pulled a train loaded with iron and passengers along a tramway at Penydarren in Wales.

title: The DNA double helix is worked out
text: This is the traditional date for the moment when Francis Crick and James Watson worked out the double-helix structure of DNA, building on X-ray work by Rosalind Franklin and others.

title: Bell's telephone patent is granted
text: The US Patent Office granted Alexander Graham Bell patent No. 174,465, the patent that covered the telephone.

title: The first telephone call
text: In Boston, Bell spoke into his new device and called his assistant Thomas Watson, who heard him clearly through the receiver in the next room.

title: A proposal for the World Wide Web
text: Tim Berners-Lee gave his boss at CERN a proposal for sharing information through linked pages, the idea that grew into the World Wide Web.

title: Herschel discovers Uranus
text: William Herschel noticed a new object in the sky that turned out to be a planet, the first one discovered with a telescope.

title: Koch announces the cause of tuberculosis
text: Robert Koch announced that tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium, a key moment for the germ theory of disease.

title: Salk announces a successful polio vaccine
text: Jonas Salk announced that his vaccine against polio had been tested successfully, offering hope of protecting children from a dreaded disease.

title: The first handheld mobile phone call
text: Martin Cooper of Motorola made a call on a prototype handheld cellular phone, a bulky ancestor of today's smartphones.

title: The first image of a black hole
text: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first picture of the shadow of a black hole, at the centre of the galaxy M87.

title: Polio vaccine declared safe and effective
text: The results of a huge field trial were announced and showed that the Salk polio vaccine was safe and worked.

title: The first YouTube video
text: Co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded 'Me at the zoo', the first video on YouTube, which lasts only about 19 seconds.

title: Bell Labs unveils the silicon solar cell
text: Researchers at Bell Laboratories announced the first practical solar cell made of silicon, able to turn sunlight into useful electricity.

title: Smallpox declared eradicated
text: The World Health Organization announced that smallpox had been wiped out, the first human disease to be eradicated.

title: Jenner's first smallpox vaccination
text: Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox material and later showed that it protected him against smallpox.

title: Patent for riveted work trousers
text: Jacob Davis and Levi Strauss received a US patent for strengthening work trousers with metal rivets, the beginning of blue jeans.

title: The Washington–Baltimore telegraph line opens
text: Samuel Morse sent the message 'What hath God wrought' from Washington to Baltimore to open the first long-distance telegraph line in the United States.

title: An eclipse tests general relativity
text: During a solar eclipse, astronomers measured how starlight bends as it passes the Sun. The results supported Einstein's theory of general relativity.

title: Marconi patents wireless telegraphy
text: Guglielmo Marconi applied for a British patent for sending signals with radio waves, without wires.

title: The Montgolfier hot-air balloon
text: The Montgolfier brothers publicly launched a large hot-air balloon in the French town of Annonay.

title: Patent for the electric iron
text: Henry Seely received a US patent for an electric flatiron that was heated by electric current instead of a fire.

title: Sholes, Glidden and Soule patent a typewriter
text: Christopher Latham Sholes, Carlos Glidden and Samuel Soule received a US patent for a typewriter, the ancestor of the QWERTY keyboard.

title: The Higgs boson announcement
text: Scientists at CERN announced the discovery of a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson, which helps explain how particles get their mass.

title: Newton publishes the Principia
text: Isaac Newton's Principia set out the laws of motion and of universal gravitation and laid the foundations of classical mechanics.

title: Dolly the sheep is born
text: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, was born at the Roslin Institute in Scotland.

title: Pasteur's first rabies vaccination
text: Louis Pasteur gave a rabies vaccine to a nine-year-old boy who had been bitten by a rabid dog. The boy survived.

title: Carrier designs modern air conditioning
text: Willis Carrier completed drawings for a system that controlled both temperature and humidity in a printing plant in Brooklyn.

title: Priestley isolates oxygen
text: Joseph Priestley heated mercury oxide and collected a gas that made flames burn brighter. It was later named oxygen.

title: IBM launches the Personal Computer
text: IBM introduced the IBM PC, which helped make computers common in offices and homes.

title: The daguerreotype is announced
text: The French government announced Louis Daguerre's photographic process and offered it as a gift to the world.

title: The first successful US oil well
text: Edwin Drake struck oil at Titusville, Pennsylvania, which started the modern petroleum industry. Oil soon supplied kerosene for lamps.

title: Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction
text: Michael Faraday saw that a changing magnetic field could make an electric current appear in a coil of wire. His discovery led to electric generators and transformers.

title: Faraday makes electricity produce motion
text: Michael Faraday showed that a wire carrying current could be made to rotate around a magnet, the first electric motor in principle.

title: Edison's Pearl Street Station starts work
text: Thomas Edison's power station in New York began supplying electricity to customers, one of the first central power stations in the world.

title: Nancy Johnson patents the ice cream freezer
text: Nancy Johnson received a US patent for a hand-cranked freezer that stirred cream inside a tub of ice and salt.

title: Howe patents the lockstitch sewing machine
text: Elias Howe received a US patent for a sewing machine that used a needle with the eye near its point to make a lockstitch.

title: The first public steam railway opens
text: The Stockton and Darlington Railway in England opened, with steam locomotives pulling passenger and goods trains.

title: Fleming notices penicillin
text: Alexander Fleming came back from holiday and saw that a mould had killed the bacteria around it on a dish, which led to the discovery of penicillin.

title: Sputnik 1 enters orbit
text: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, which opened the space age.

title: A patent for microwave cooking
text: Raytheon filed a patent application based on Percy Spencer's discovery that microwaves could cook food, which led to the microwave oven.

title: Breaking the sound barrier
text: Test pilot Chuck Yeager flew the Bell X-1 faster than the speed of sound in level flight.

title: The first ARPANET message
text: The first message between two computers, at UCLA and the Stanford Research Institute, was sent over the ARPANET, the forerunner of the Internet. The system crashed after the first two letters.

title: Röntgen discovers X-rays
text: Wilhelm Röntgen noticed a mysterious glow and found invisible rays that pass through paper, wood and flesh to make images of bones.

title: The first free flight by humans
text: Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes flew over Paris in a Montgolfier hot-air balloon.

title: 'On the Origin of Species' is published
text: Charles Darwin's book explained evolution by natural selection and changed biology for ever.

title: ChatGPT is released
text: OpenAI released ChatGPT to the public. The chatbot quickly became one of the fastest-growing apps in history.

title: The first nuclear chain reaction
text: Enrico Fermi's team at the University of Chicago started the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.

title: Dunlop patents the pneumatic tyre
text: John Boyd Dunlop was granted a British patent for an air-filled rubber tyre, which he had first made to give his son's tricycle a smoother ride.

title: A radio signal across the Atlantic
text: Guglielmo Marconi reported hearing the Morse letter 'S' in Newfoundland, sent from Cornwall across the Atlantic Ocean.

title: The Wright brothers fly
text: At Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first powered, controlled flights of a heavier-than-air machine.

title: The first basketball game
text: James Naismith's students played the first game of basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts, using peach baskets as goals.

title: The transistor is demonstrated
text: Scientists at Bell Labs demonstrated the first working transistor, the tiny switch at the heart of modern electronics.

title: Cochrane patents the dishwasher
text: Josephine Cochrane received a US patent for a dishwasher in which a motor sprayed soapy water onto dishes held in wire racks.

title: The first public film screening
text: The Lumière brothers showed moving pictures to a paying audience in a Paris café, a key moment in the history of cinema.
